name: What is the difference between a detached and attached room addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an attached and detached room addition, and when does each make sense?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between an attached and detached room addition, and when does each make sense?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached room addition expands the main house and usually feels like a natural extension of the existing floor plan. It is often the better choice when the goal is to add a bedroom, suite, office, or living area that connects closely to the rest of the home. A detached addition works better when privacy matters, such as for a guest house, studio, or separate workspace. Detached projects may offer more separation from the main house but can also require additional utility planning and site coordination. In Los Angeles, the choice depends on available lot space, zoning, setbacks, and how the space will be used day to day. Attached additions often provide a stronger resale story because they increase the main home’s square footage. Detached structures can still add value, especially when they are well designed and permitted, but they serve a different purpose.
acceptedAnswer.description: An attached addition connects directly to the existing house, while a detached addition is a separate structure on the property. Attached additions usually improve daily access and resale value more directly, while detached additions offer privacy and flexibility for guest space or work-from-home use.
